posts.name: Notion Developer Platform
posts.tagline: Build on Notion, not just inside it
posts.description: Notion Developer Platform lets teams build on Notion with CLI, Workers, database syncs, agent tools, webhook triggers, MCP, and External Agents APIs, so data, workflows, and agents can operate inside the same shared workspace.

comments.body:
Hi everyone!

Notion used to be a place to work in. Now it’s a place to build on.

This release makes Notion more than a workspace and closer to agent infrastructure. By introducing hosted Workers and a dedicated CLI, developers can now deploy data syncs (like @Zendesk or @Linear) and custom agent tools entirely on Notion's infrastructure.

With External Agents API, you can now bring your own agents—whether it's Claude, Codex, or an in-house build—directly into your workspace. They operate as first-class collaborators that your team can mention, assign tasks to, and review.

The Developer Platform unlocks the full potential of agents for your entire team. What will you build?

Why?
Why not focus on fixing the editor and the slugginess first?!

As a developer .... I feel like Notion is an incredible workspace tool for note-taking, but it is fundamentally not built to be a reliable production database or a headless CMS.

Has anyone actually managed to build a stable, scalable production app on top of Notion without losing their mind?

Think about my biggest pain points:

  • Expiring S3 Media URLs == game over

  • The block payload is worse than walking on magma

  • API Ratelimits is 3/s

What does your caching infrastructure look like?
the landing page is next-level

This is the launch I didn't expect from Notion but makes complete sense in hindsight. Workers filling the gap between what MCP covers and what custom logic actually needs that's the right architectural call.

I set up a Worker that syncs a Zendesk ticket feed into a Notion DB and it took maybe 15 minutes.

But obervability is req as when a worker fails mid-run, the error logs are minimal, you get a status but not enough context to debug quickly. Coming from serverless environments, I'd expect at least a structured log stream per execution. That's the one thing that would make me comfortable running this in production rather than just experiments.
This looks pretty neat. Can you integrate custom code snippets directly, or is it more about using pre-built templates?

The dedicated CLI for deploying custom agent tools is exactly what was missing for serious builds. I love the idea of agents as first-class collaborators you can actually 'assign' tasks to. Does the API allow the agent to report back its 'reasoning' steps within the Notion comment thread, or is it strictly focused on the final output/task completion?
It’s really pulling me in!

posts.name: Notion 3.4
posts.tagline: New dashboards, connectors, sidebar & smarter AI agents
posts.description: Notion now generates images, builds dashboards, and presents your docs without leaving the workspace. 10+ features shipped for operators, PMs, and teams scaling on AI.

comments.body:
Notion 3.4 feels like a major step toward the “all-in-one AI workspace” vision 👀

  • New dashboard view turns scattered databases into clean KPI and metrics hubs without messy linked views

  • Redesigned sidebar helps reduce clutter and improve focus

  • Presentation mode lets you present directly from Notion docs

  • Tabs block makes organizing content cleaner and easier

  • AI can now generate charts, slides, diagrams, and visuals right inside your workspace

  • Archive pages improve search quality and AI responses

What makes this different: Everything stays connected inside one workflow instead of switching between multiple tools for docs, dashboards, presentations, and AI creation.

P.S. I hunt the latest and greatest launches in tech, SaaS and AI, follow to be notified → @rohanrecommends

The dashboard view was the missing piece for Notion as a real ops tool. Curious how the AI chart generation handles ambiguous data — does it ask for clarification or just makes a call? That's usually the UX challenge with AI-generated visuals
The AI generating charts and diagrams is interesting! How does Notion's AI handle data privacy — do the generated visuals stay local or get processed in the cloud?

The dashboard-from-databases play is the right one — most knowledge tools die when they remain a stack of documents instead of becoming a state surface for the project. Once a CFO can read project-finance economics off a Notion dashboard the way they read off a finance model, the workspace stops being a wiki and starts being the source of truth. We've been chasing the same shape on ModeLoop (modeloop.net/?i=1) for project-finance models — the value isn't the cells, it's the dashboard layer that compresses 200 tabs into one IRR and three sensitivities. Question: how do Notion 3.4's dashboards handle versioning when underlying database rows change retroactively? That's the painful part in finance — restating a number a month later is a different operation than updating it forward.

posts.name: SyncBank
posts.tagline: Automatically sync banks to Notion, Airtable, Sheets & more.
posts.description: Sync EU bank transactions to Notion, Google Sheets, Airtable, Actual Budget, or CSV. Built for anyone tired of CSV imports, messy transaction data, and finance subscriptions. SyncBank is a self-hosted Docker bridge: your data stays on your machine, with no cloud sync, a one-time payment, and flexible mappings to fit your workflow. Connect via PSD2/Open Banking using Enable Banking, a GoCardless/Nordigen alternative.

comments.body:
Hey Product Hunt 👋

I'm Sam, and I want to share the real story behind SyncBank — because it didn't start as a product. It started as a personal project to solve a problem.

A few years ago I decided to track my financial life inside Notion. It worked beautifully… except for one part: every week I'd open my bank's website, download a CSV, fix dates, remove duplicates, rename columns, and paste everything in. Only 20 minutes, but the kind of task I kept postponing — until the data was already stale.

I tried a lot of existing tools. Some, like YNAB or Copilot, were great — but they meant yet another monthly subscription, and not a cheap one. Others kept my bank data inside someone else's cloud. Many were full budgeting apps trying to replace my setup. The real issue: I already had a finance system I liked. I just wanted my transactions to arrive there automatically.

I also tried Actual Budget and saw many EU users relied on GoCardless/Nordigen to connect their banks. That looked perfect — until I realized I was too late. From July 2025, GoCardless stopped accepting new Bank Account Data accounts.

That's when SyncBank started.

Today, SyncBank is a self-hosted Docker app that connects to EU banks via PSD2/Open Banking through Enable Banking, and syncs transactions to one destination of your choice: Notion, Google Sheets, Airtable, Actual Budget, or CSV.

Honest note: even though it supports five destinations, most people will probably use just one — the place where their financial life already lives. I sync to Notion, and that's it.

I'd love your feedback. Are you still importing CSVs manually, using a budgeting app, or keeping your finance setup updated somewhere else?

Even a quick "I use X, but Y is annoying" would help me understand what to improve next.

SyncBank won't stop here, I'll keep adding features and destinations based on real user requests, so if something is missing for your workflow, let me know.

Thanks for reading, and thanks in advance for any feedback, even the critical kind.
I can’t believe I’ll never have to go through a thousand steps again and that everything’s gonna be automatic in my Excel!

I’m a (happy) Finance Tracker Pro user, can’t wait to test SyncBank in Notion. 

Greetings from Italy!
Looks cool. Is there a CLI or MCP I can get my AI agents to use. I want to run all kinds of automations and analyses on my bank data.
Awesome idea! Can’t wait to try it! Would love to be able to connect with my Brazilian accts!
finalmente posso sincronizzare la mia transazione automaticamente su Google sheets
Hi, could it help users on building a conciliation process between QB online and Banking Statements?

I’ve been manually importing CSV files from my bank for years and it’s been a nightmare. But SyncBank just handles it. Transactions show up in my Notion automatically, no more wasted Sunday afternoons cleaning up spreadsheets 🥲

posts.name: NotionReminder
posts.tagline: Never miss Notion deadlines: Send alerts via Slack & Email
posts.description: Stop paying expensive per-task fees on Zapier just to track Notion dates. NotionReminder is a dedicated micro-SaaS that turns your databases into an automated alert engine. Unlike generic tools, it runs continuously in the background to monitor date columns and dispatches alerts to Slack or Email. It features smart date monitoring, flexible channel routing, and a centralized Action Ledger to verify every sent notification.

comments.body:
Hi Product Hunt! 👋 I’m the creator of NotionReminder.

Like many of you, I rely on Notion for everything but I kept running into the same exact wall when it came to tracking time-sensitive information.

The Breaking Point
Notion is a brilliant operational hub, but it has a fundamental blind spot: it cannot trigger external alerts based on the passive passage of time. Because its native automations are strictly event-driven, a critical deadline can arrive on the calendar in complete silence unless someone actively edits the page.

To fix this, teams usually resort to duct-tape solutions: building complex Zapier flows that silently break if a column name changes, burning through unpredictable Notion AI credits just to check dates or relying entirely on human memory.

The Philosophy
I realized we didn’t need another bloated workflow tool. We needed a deterministic, single-purpose chronological alerts engine. Something that runs quietly in the background, handles schema changes elegantly and never drops the ball.

Meet NotionReminder
I built this tool to secure your mission-critical operational data. We poll your databases in the background and deliver flawless, beautifully formatted notifications to your team exactly when you need them.

Who gets the most out of this?
✅ Freelancers & Solopreneurs staying on top of client deliverables, content calendars and individual subscription renewals.
✅ IT & Ops tracking SSL certificates and domain renewals.
✅ HR & People Ops monitoring legally binding visas and employee contracts.
✅ Founders & RevOps keeping an eye on SaaS renewals to stop bleeding budget.
✅ Agencies & Account Execs needing automated invoice follow-ups.

How the engine works:
⏳ Dynamic Time Thresholds: Tell the engine to alert your team precisely 90, 60, or 30 days *before* a contract renews or an invoice is due.
💬 Rich Multi-Channel Dispatch: No more parsing ugly JSON. NotionReminder dynamically translates your database properties into beautifully formatted Slack Block Kit messages and HTML emails.
🛡️ Idempotent Delivery: Our immutable internal state ledger ensures an alert for a specific record and threshold is sent exactly once. End notification spam.
🧠 Auto-Resetting: If you manually update a date in Notion after an alert fires, the system detects the change and seamlessly resets the ledger for the new deadline.

I'm super excited to share this with the Product Hunt community today. You can try our Hobby Tier completely free and we only charge a predictable flat rate when your volume demands it.

I’ll be hanging out in the comments all day. I’d love to know: what kind of mission-critical dates are you currently tracking manually in your workspace?

Cheers! 🎉
